hints.title: Calculating Order Frequency per Product
hints.text: Count orders grouped by customer_id and product_id to determine how many times each customer purchased each item.

hints.title: Ranking Frequencies with Ties
hints.text: use rank() over (partition by customer_id order by count(*) desc) so tied maximum frequencies all receive rank 1.

hints.title: Joining Product Catalog
hints.text: join the ranked CTE with Products on product_id and filter where rank is 1.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
WITH ProductFreq AS (
    SELECT customer_id,
           product_id,
           COUNT(*) AS cnt,
           RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS rnk
    FROM Orders
    GROUP BY customer_id, product_id
)
SELECT pf.customer_id, pf.product_id, p.product_name
FROM ProductFreq pf
JOIN Products p ON pf.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE pf.rnk = 1;
```

complexity.notes: Aggregates product frequencies per customer and computes partitioned ranks in O(O log O) time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Row number discards tied most frequent products arbitrarily.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Rank preserves all co-optimal frequent purchases.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use of rank() over row_number() to retain all tied entries.

import pandas as pd

def most_frequently_ordered_products(customers: pd.DataFrame, orders: pd.DataFrame, products: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    counts = orders.groupby(['customer_id', 'product_id']).size().reset_index(name='cnt')
    counts['rnk'] = counts.groupby('customer_id')['cnt'].rank(method='min', ascending=False)
    top = counts[counts['rnk'] == 1].merge(products, on='product_id')
    return top[['customer_id', 'product_id', 'product_name']]
